children: Life360's third-quarter result looks good to its bull at Jefferies, especially given low investor expectations ahead of the announcement. Analyst Roger Samuel tells clients in a note that the location-app developer's key performance indicators were slightly ahead of consensus, flagging better-than-expected user growth and earnings. He acknowledges that operating expenses of US$126 million were about US$4 million higher than anticipated, but points out that opex as a percentage of revenue fell to 72%, from 80% in the prior quarter. Jefferies has a last-published buy rating on Life360's Australia-listed stock, with a target price of 30.00 Australian dollars. Shares are down 8.9% at A$20.34. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
